checks.def2_finding: Verified against the scan (journal p. 233 last line / p. 234 first line): « s'il existe une application l' de T(A) dans T(B) telle que … l(M+m)=l(M)+l'(m) ». The literal reading admits l' merely additive, and not_isAffinePrinted_imp_affine exhibits l : ℝ → ℝ (ℚ-linear, l 1 = 0, l √2 ≠ 0) satisfying the printed definition with ¬∃ f : ℝ →ᵃ[ℝ] ℝ, ⇑f = l. The proof is sound (hlin derives l x = x·l 1 from f.linear's ℝ-linearity). isAffinePrinted_and_continuous_iff (continuity forces ℝ-linearity via AddMonoidHom.toRealLinearMap) and the finite-dimensional variant are correct and stated at the right generality (real normed affine spaces). affineFunction_iff covers the Exemple (l' in the dual) over any commutative ring
checks.charitable_reading: The finding DISSOLVES under a charitable reading, and the paper supplies it: (1) Déf. 2 opens « T(A) et T(B) les espaces vectoriels définis sur un même corps » — the common field matters only if l' is linear; for an arbitrary map it is idle; (2) the Exemple right after asks « un élément l' du dual de T(A) », i.e. linear; (3) GA(n, R) (p. 236) is the group of automorphisms of the affine structure, which every later use (Groups.lean's GAR = AffineEquiv) reads as affine-linear. The counterexample also needs the axiom of choice: every measurable, or locally bounded, solution is affine, so no explicit l exists. The literal statement is genuinely broader, so the counterexample is worth keeping; but it is an omitted word, of the [sic] kind, not a mathematical error

issues.problem: The finding is presented as the paper being wrong ('strictly weaker than an affine map'). The paper's own wording (« sur un même corps », and the Exemple's « élément du dual ») shows l' is meant linear; the literal reading is an omitted « linéaire », and the counterexample is necessarily non-constructive (choice; no measurable or locally bounded witness exists). Presented as is, a reader may think Benzécri's affine geometry is unsound
issues.fix: Reword the finding: 'Déf. 2 omits « linéaire » before « application l' »; the intent is evident from « sur un même corps » (l.150) and the Exemple (l.161–162). Literally read, the definition admits non-affine (non-measurable, choice-dependent) maps: not_isAffinePrinted_imp_affine.' Keep the theorem. Add to questions whether the author treats this as a [sic]-level slip (then the evident reading governs)

fidelity_summary: Déf. 1 is the paper's definition, as printed (empty A included), with a two-way bridge to Mathlib's AddTorsor; the mark is earned. Déf. 2 is formalized literally, the gap between the literal and the intended notion is proved both ways (counterexample without continuity, equivalence with continuity), and the Exemple is exactly Mathlib's AffineMap to the scalars. No vacuous hypothesis, no definitional trivialisation.
